items.title: 2-bit copy in VRAM + exact residual in system RAM as the verifier: speculative decoding for models that don't fit your GPU
items.excerpt: Hi Guys!, Recently I was making a research and development, but I do not have time to go further with this idea (kids, work, etc.). But maybe it will be interesting for someone. I do not think it would be something big, but maybe interesting approach that can be used in some of the cases. I believe that it is not AI slop, you can use those information's and try by yourself using Claude or Astra. The idea was my own and I am using it in my production app, it saved me a lot of money (project is not related to LLM's). Not sure if it is outdated or not, it can work also with MTP. Please, just don’t be unkind. I’m sharing my idea with you, and anyone is welcome to experiment with it. TLDR: Keep a 2-bit version of the model on the GPU and the rest of the weights (the residual, 6-8 bit) in system RAM. The 2-bit copy drafts tokens, then the full model checks them: the GPU does the 2-bit part, the CPU does the residual part, and only activations go over PCIe. So the draft costs no extra memory, it's literally half of the verifier. What I measured (real weights, but dequantized and run in PyTorch, so no tok/s yet): - 2-bit + 8-bit residual is closer to bf16 than Q8_0, about half
